chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn al-Muthanna, from Sadeyr, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
Begin with Makkah and end with us.

key_terms.ابْدَءُوا: Begin (imperative plural), indicating the starting point of the journey
key_terms.اخْتِمُوا: End/Conclude (imperative plural), indicating the final destination
key_terms.بِنَا: With us (referring to the Imams/Ahl al-Bayt), indicating their presence in Medina
key_terms.مَكَّةَ: Makkah, the city of the Kaaba and the primary destination for Hajj

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of ending a Hajj journey with a visit to the Imams in Medina?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (peace be upon him) establishes a spiritual protocol for pilgrims, instructing them to commence their journey in Makkah and conclude it with the Ahl al-Bayt in Medina. This directive underscores the Shia scholarly view that visiting the Imams is not merely a supplementary act but an integral completion of the Hajj ritual, linking the divine covenant of the Kaaba with the earthly representatives of God. It reflects the historical practice of early Shia communities who prioritized the 'Ziyarat al-Imam' as a means of solidifying their connection to the Prophet's lineage after fulfilling the pillar of Hajj.
